evidence.note: CONFIRMED:  stores a title raw, and viewers_lists._line renders r['title'] verbatim, so a title holding ESC[31m/OSC reach the terminal. Fix: strip ANSI CSI/OSC + C0/C1 controls in _line; tested test_viewers_strip_control.py
followed r-task-phase-needs-wave, D-everything-configurable; regression test added
_CONTROL regex strips ANSI CSI/OSC + C0 controls; _line applies it to r['title']

chunk_findings.detail: The stripper drops ESC but leaves CR and LF (`\x0d`/`\x0a` are outside `[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f\x9b\x9c]`), so a title still drives the terminal. For `title="ok\r  Tfake            open       owned"`, `_line` emits that CR; on a real tty the cursor returns to column 0 and the rest of the title overwrites the row, so the operator sees a forged task line instead of the real id/state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:_CONTROL

chunk_findings.detail: C1 introducers other than CSI/ST are not removed, despite the class treating U+009B/U+009C as live controls. Given `title="\x9d0;pwned\x07"` (C1 OSC + BEL), `sub` only deletes BEL and leaves U+009D plus `0;pwned`. On an 8-bit (non-UTF-8) terminal that byte starts an OSC, the same class of replay the CSI/OSC arms are meant to stop. U+0090 (DCS) and U+009F (APC) are likewise passed through.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:_CONTROL
